h1: Forgotten Hostel Silom — Bangkok's Best-Located Budget Hostel Near Samyan Mitrtown & Banthat Thong
intro: Picture stepping out of your hostel, walking five minutes down Sap Road in Bang Rak, and arriving at Samyan Mitrtown for your morning coffee — then wandering to the legendary Banthat Thong food strip in the evening for boat noodles, shabu, and street-side desserts that cost next to nothing. Forgotten Hostel Silom is a 3-star, 46-room hostel that opened in 2023 (refreshed in 2024) and draws backpackers and budget business travelers with a location that pricier hotels in the same neighborhood charge five to ten times more to match. Dorm beds from approx ฿450, mixed dorms from ฿550, private en-suite doubles around ฿1,100/night. Score 8.6 from 1,051 Trip.com reviews — led by near-perfect marks for location and staff friendliness.

body.html: Who is Forgotten Hostel Silom for? Despite the wistful name, there is nothing forgotten about this place — it is a freshly renovated hostel that opened in 2023 on the third floor of a building on Sap Road in Bang Rak, a neighborhood that sits squarely between the student energy of Samyan and the business bustle of Silom. The hostel targets solo backpackers, travel pairs, and budget-conscious professionals who prioritize location above everything else. If you are willing to share a bathroom in a dorm to pocket the savings, or splash a modest ฿1,100 for a private room with an en-suite, this is one of the best-value beds you will find anywhere near this stretch of Bangkok's Blue MRT line. Compiled from 1,051 real guest reviews on Trip.com (score: 8.6 / 10), the picture is consistent: guests are surprised by how much they get for the price, and the location regularly earns the single highest category score (8.9 / 10).

Location and Getting Around — The hostel sits at 3rd Floor, 5 Sap Road, Si Phraya, Bang Rak, Bangkok 10500. MRT Sam Yan station is approximately 390 metres away — a five-minute walk at most. From Sam Yan you can ride the Blue Line north to Hua Lamphong, Lumpini, Silom, and on towards the interchange at Asok for the Sukhumvit corridor, or south into the suburbs. The practical upshot: nearly every major Bangkok attraction is reachable by rail without a taxi. Samyan Mitrtown, the mall built atop the MRT station, sits about 500 metres from the hostel door and houses a supermarket, food court, coffee shops, and a late-night pharmacy — genuinely useful for early-morning check-ins and late-night arrivals. The Banthat Thong Road food strip, a Bangkok institution packed with boat noodles, small-pot shabu, shaved ice desserts, and dozens of other local dishes at street prices, is roughly 10 minutes on foot. One caveat noted in several reviews: Sap Road sees moderate traffic noise at night, so light sleepers staying in a dorm should pack earplugs or request a room on the quieter side.
"Great location — walked to the MRT in under five minutes. Staff were incredibly friendly and helpful. Room was clean and the bed was comfortable. Excellent value for money in Bangkok."

Room Types and What to Expect — Forgotten Hostel Silom runs 46 rooms across three broad categories. At the entry level, Female-Only Dorm (Lady Dorm) beds — both upper and lower bunks — start from approximately ฿450–500 per night, making them the cheapest reliable sleep within walking distance of Sam Yan MRT. Mixed Dormitory beds run approximately ฿500–600 per night; some rooms hold up to 12 bunks, so if you have done dormitory travel before, you know what that means in terms of noise and elbow room. For those who want a door they can close, the Private Double Room with an en-suite bathroom costs around ฿1,100 per night — a price that would make many guesthouses blush given the location. Guest reviews confirm the rooms are air-conditioned, Wi-Fi-equipped, and clean, with the private doubles noted to have a small balcony in some configurations. The hostel was renovated in 2024, which has improved the general condition of fixtures and bedding relative to earlier reviews.

Facilities and Common Areas — For a hostel at this price point, the amenity list is solid. Highlights include a shared kitchen for self-catering, a communal lounge, and a co-working space that makes this viable for digital nomads passing through. There is an on-site restaurant and bar serving Thai and international food, useful for evenings when you do not want to venture out. Practical staples — 24-hour reception, luggage storage, multilingual staff, laundry service, and free Wi-Fi — are all present. Reviewers specifically praise the Wi-Fi reliability, which matters when you need to sort onward bookings or catch up on work. There is no swimming pool or fitness room, and breakfast is not included in the room rate; you will need to order from the restaurant or step out, which given the food options nearby is no hardship at all.

What Real Guests Say — Honest Pros and Cons — Across 1,051 Trip.com reviews, the category breakdown gives location 8.9, service 8.8, cleanliness 8.5, and amenities 8.3. That gap between location/service and amenities is the honest story of this hostel. Repeated praise: staff described as "incredibly friendly," "helpful and accommodating," and "always smiling"; the location praised as "perfect" for accessing the MRT, Samyan Mitrtown, and the food streets; rooms described as "clean and bright" with "soft, comfortable beds" post-renovation; and the value-for-money proposition called "unbeatable" for central Bangkok. Repeated criticism: noise is the number-one complaint — both street-level traffic and dormitory disturbances from other guests; some earlier reviews flagged broken lockers (management indicated these were addressed in the 2024 renovation, but worth checking on arrival); a minority of reviews raised concerns about ventilation in larger dorms; and one review reported a theft incident, a reminder that personal valuables in any hostel dorm should be secured at all times. Taken together: the hostel earns its 8.6 through location and team, not through luxury.

"Every corner was clean and bright, the beds were soft and comfortable, and the toilet and shower were separate and spotless. Loved the small balcony in our private room. The walk to MRT Sam Yan was genuinely five minutes. Will come back."

Food and Neighbourhood Life — The hostel's restaurant and bar handles dinner and a drink, but the real draw is the food scene surrounding the building. Samyan Mitrtown (five-minute walk) has a full food court and a late-opening TopLine supermarket. The Banthat Thong Road strip (ten minutes on foot) is one of Bangkok's great street-food runs: boat noodles in tiny earthenware pots, Thai-style shabu, papaya salad stalls, grilled pork skewers, and shaved-ice shops side by side. Prices are very much local rates — a full meal for under ฿100 is common. Chamchuri Square, another ten-minute walk in the other direction, adds coffee shops and sit-down restaurants for days when air-conditioning is non-negotiable. Chinatown (Yaowarat Road) is two MRT stops away for evening eating; Silom and its night market are a similar short ride in the other direction.

Value and Comparison — The Sam Yan–Bang Rak corridor is one of Bangkok's most central and convenient sub-districts, but hotel rates here reflect that: mid-range options like Triple Y Hotel or dusitD2 Samyan start at ฿2,800–3,000 per night for a standard room. Forgotten Hostel Silom occupies a completely different bracket — ฿450 for a dorm bed, ฿1,100 for a private room — while sitting within the same five-minute MRT radius. For budget travelers who are comfortable with a hostel format, this is difficult to beat. For those who want a private room but cannot stretch to full hotel pricing, the ฿1,100 Private Double with en-suite is quietly one of the better deals in the city. The trade-off, to be clear, is the dormitory-level noise environment and the absence of hotel amenities. That trade-off is entirely the traveler's to weigh.

Summary — Who Should Book and What to Know First — Forgotten Hostel Silom is the strongest budget option within walking distance of MRT Sam Yan, and the 8.6 score from more than 1,000 real guests reflects a property that delivers on its core promises of location, cleanliness, and friendly service. Book it if you are a solo backpacker, a travel pair on a tight budget, or someone staying in Bangkok for a hospital visit at King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital or meetings in the Silom business district. Think twice if you are sensitive to noise (opt for the private room rather than a large dorm), expect hotel-standard amenities, or want guaranteed peace and quiet after midnight. Practical tip: book ahead for the November–January high season, when rooms at this price level in this location sell out quickly.

tips.title: Use MRT Sam Yan as Your Base
tips.body: Sam Yan station is five minutes away and puts the whole Blue Line at your feet — Hua Lamphong, Lumpini, Silom, Asok interchange, all without hailing a taxi or sitting in Bangkok traffic.

tips.title: Walk to Banthat Thong Road
tips.body: Ten minutes on foot and you hit one of Bangkok's classic street-food strips. Boat noodles, Thai shabu, papaya salad, and shaved-ice shops open from morning to late at night, all at local prices.

tips.title: Secure Your Valuables
tips.body: As with any hostel anywhere in the world: lock your valuables in a locker (check it works on arrival) and keep a padlock or combination lock of your own. Most guests have no issues — one report in a thousand is a reminder, not a pattern.

tips.title: Choose Private if Noise Bothers You
tips.body: The dormitory noise concern is consistent across reviews. For a few hundred baht more, the Private Double with an en-suite bathroom is quiet enough for a proper night's sleep — and at ฿1,100 it is still exceptional value for this part of Bangkok.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Forgotten Hostel Silom Bangkok

faq.q: Where is Forgotten Hostel Silom and how do I get there?
faq.a: The hostel is at 3rd Floor, 5 Sap Road, Si Phraya, Bang Rak, Bangkok 10500. MRT Sam Yan station is approximately 390 metres away — a five-minute walk. The Blue Line connects directly to Hua Lamphong, Lumpini, Silom, and the Asok interchange for Sukhumvit. Samyan Mitrtown mall is about 500 m from the hostel. Banthat Thong food street is 10 minutes on foot.

faq.q: What are the room types and prices at Forgotten Hostel Silom?
faq.a: Female-only dorm beds start from approximately ฿450–500 per night. Mixed dormitory beds are around ฿500–600. Private Double Room with en-suite bathroom is approximately ฿1,100 per night. Prices rise during the November–January high season and on long weekends — book ahead and compare platforms for the best rate.

faq.q: How noisy is Forgotten Hostel Silom?
faq.a: Noise is the most common complaint in real guest reviews. Street traffic on Sap Road can be heard at night, and large dormitory rooms (up to 12 beds) naturally generate their own noise. Light sleepers are advised to request a quieter room, choose the Private Double, or pack earplugs for the dorm.

faq.q: What facilities does Forgotten Hostel Silom have?
faq.a: The hostel has a shared kitchen, communal lounge, co-working space, restaurant and bar, 24-hour reception, luggage storage, free Wi-Fi, and laundry service. There is no swimming pool, no fitness room, and no breakfast included in the room rate. Food is available from the on-site restaurant or a 5–10-minute walk to Samyan Mitrtown or Banthat Thong Road.

faq.q: Is Forgotten Hostel Silom good value for Bangkok?
faq.a: For the location — walking distance from MRT Sam Yan, Samyan Mitrtown, and Banthat Thong food street — yes, it is very good value. Hotels in the same neighbourhood start at ฿2,800–3,000/night. A dorm bed here at ฿450 or a private room at ฿1,100 with a score of 8.6 from 1,051 real reviews is a strong proposition for budget-conscious travellers who are comfortable with a hostel format.
